purpose: Celastrol dissolution/solubility/degradation evidence for the released-API layer. Qualitative consensus recorded; NUMERIC values NOT recorded until a primary is opened (search returned figures but no full text opened here).

qualitative_consensus.reactivity: quinone-methide Michael acceptor - binds thiols (mechanistic + instability basis)
qualitative_consensus.status: SECONDARY_REVIEW / consensus - NOT a measured value in this project

numeric_values_NOT_recorded.reason: web search returned candidate numbers (e.g. an aqueous-solubility figure, a beta-CD 30-fold enhancement, a 96h degradation %) but NO primary/full text was opened; recording them would violate the no-numbers-from-search rule
needed_primary: celastrol equilibrium aqueous solubility vs pH (37 C)
celastrol degradation kinetics (t90) under physiological/oxidative conditions

released_celastrol_fate_by_environment.release_medium_2_8_ethanol_PBS: co-solvent maintains sink (Chen release/permeation medium) - not physiological
released_celastrol_fate_by_environment.stratum_corneum: lipophilic - celastrol likely partitions into SC lipids (qualitative; celastrol is lipophilic)
released_celastrol_fate_by_environment.rule: do NOT apply one environment's behaviour universally; each is a separate, mostly-unknown state

supporting_solubilization_systems.effect: SBE-betaCD complexation reported to enhance solubility & reduce degradation (values UNVERIFIED)
supporting_solubilization_systems.relevance: evidence that celastrol precipitation/degradation is real and formulation-mitigable

modelability: released-celastrol dissolution/precipitation is at most a QUALITATIVE risk layer (S1). A quantitative supersaturation-precipitation model (type E) is NOT supported - required solubility/pH/dissolution/nucleation data are not opened.
